question.knowledge_point: Finding an Entry of a Matrix
question.problem:
Find the entry ${e}_{31}$ of the matrix $E$, where 

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 5 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
The entry ${e}_{31}$ lies at the intersection of the $3$rd row and $1$st column. Therefore, ${e}_{31}=-3.$

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 5 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

evidence.solution_quote: The entry ${e}_{31}$ lies at the intersection of the $3$rd row and $1$st column. Therefore, ${e}_{31}=-3.$

question.knowledge_point: Finding an Entry of a Square Matrix
question.problem:
Find the entry ${b}_{32}$ of the matrix $B$, where 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
The entry ${b}_{32}$ should lie at the intersection of the $3$rd row and $2$nd column. 
Since $B$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix, it does not have the $3$rd row. 

Therefore, $B$ does not have the entry ${b}_{32}.$

evidence.solution_quote: Therefore, $B$ does not have the entry ${b}_{32}.$
